title: What the peer-reviewed hypomagnetic-field literature actually establishes about magnetic-field effects on mitochondrial and ROS endpoints
question: Which measurable biological endpoints (e.g. mitochondrial respiration / membrane potential, ROS/superoxide proxies, cell viability) have replicate peer-reviewed evidence for alteration when the ambient field is changed from a geomagnetic baseline (~25-60 uT) to a hypomagnetic field (~nT range), what effect sizes and known confounds (temperature, vibration, oxygen, light, radical-pair vs magnetite mechanisms) are reported, and where is the literature contested or non-replicated — so that NOXIA's magnetobiology research vertical slice (baseline 45 uT vs 5 nT exposure, endpoints mitochondrial_respiration/superoxide_proxy, claimType 'magnetic_environment_affects_measured_biological_endpoint', confidence 0.35, status 'testing') is calibrated to the real evidence and its unresolved status is not flattened into a settled result by the research-exchange canonization path?
why_now: The magnetobiology vertical slice is live in code (lib/game/cognition/runtime.ts createMagnetobiologyExperiment; values in lib/game/cognition/magnetobiologyResearch.test.ts) and feeds the shared research-exchange / evidence-assessment contracts. Its declared external evidence backstop, OTA-SCI-0096-2026-DE, is not present in this repository, and the code itself already refuses to assert human, therapeutic or habitat effects — making the strength (or absence) of the cellular evidence the decisive externally checkable question.
real_world_anchor: Hypomagnetic-field biology and magnetoreception/magnetobiology: peer-reviewed reports of nT-range field effects on mitochondrial activity, membrane potential and reactive-oxygen-species/superoxide in cellular and animal models, against Earth's ~25-60 uT geomagnetic baseline, including radical-pair and magnetite mechanism reviews and replication disputes.
novelty_reason: No previous topic concerned cellular magnetobiology. Prior medicine-adjacent work covered human partial-gravity adaptation and reproduction (RES-20260913-CF5AF859) and life-support/habitability parameters (RES-20260828-79092FF4); neither addresses magnetic-field exposure effects on cellular endpoints, so this is a materially distinct evidence question.
